newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Jan real earnings fell 2.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Jan real earnings fell 2.0 pct.

text.p: Average weekly earnings of U.S. workers, after adjusting for inflation and seasonal factors, fell 2.0 percent in January, the biggest drop in more than 23 years, the Labor Department said Wednesday.
The January decrease, the largest monthly decline since a 2.2 percent plunge in August 1973, followed a revised 0.8 percent rise in December real average weekly earnings.
Previously, the Labor Department reported that December real earnings rose 1.1 percent.
Wall Street economists had expected January real average weekly earnings to fall 1.5 percent.

The January drop was due to a 2.0 percent fall in average weekly hours, the department said. A 0.1 percent rise in average hourly earnings was offset by 0.1 percent drop in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, it said.
Real average weekly earnings in January were still 2.0 percent above their January 1996 level, the department said.

In constant 1982 dollars, weekly earnings for non-supervisory private workers outside the farm sector averaged a seasonally adjusted $254.49 in January, versus $259.81 in December and $250.33 in January 1996.
In current dollars, weekly earnings averaged a seasonally adjusted $411.25 in January, compared with $419.34 in December and $392.76 in January last year.
